children.label: b
children.prompt: Approximate $\displaystyle\int_9^{16}\sqrt{x}\,dx$, using the trapezoidal rule with the eight function values above. Give your answer correct to three significant figures.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the exact value of $\displaystyle\int_9^{16}\sqrt{x}\,dx$?

children.label: d
children.prompt: Show that the second derivative of $y=x^{1/2}$ is $y''=-\frac14x^{-3/2}$, and use this result to explain why the unrounded trapezoidal approximation is less than the value of the definite integral.

answer.short: $y''=-\frac14x^{-3/2}<0$ on $[9,16]$. The curve is concave down, so its chords lie below it and the trapezoidal approximation is an underestimate.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=x^{1/2}\\y'&=\frac12x^{-1/2}\\y''&=-\frac14x^{-3/2}\end{aligned}$$
For $x>0$, $y''<0$, so the curve is concave down on $[9,16]$. The chords lie below the curve, so the trapezoidal approximation is less than the exact integral. Compare the unrounded values: $24.6633<\frac{74}{3}\approx24.6667$. Rounding the approximation to $24.7$ hides this difference.
